## Anomaly Localization (If Detected)
No genuine double-counting into a common aggregation node was found. All variables flagged in the structural reference data as "consumed by more than one operation" (i_2–i_7, o_10, o_11, o_13, o_15, o_17, o_19, o_21) were individually traced end-to-end to the terminal output `o_26` (sample standard deviation), which is the sole leaf variable in the graph.

- `i_2`…`i_7` (the six raw sample values) are each consumed exactly twice: once inside the `addBulk` (`op_1`) that produces the sum `o_8`, and once inside their own individual `subtract` operation (`op_3`, `op_5`, `op_7`, `op_9`, `op_11`, `op_13`) that computes their own deviation from the mean. These are two *different* statistical quantities (the sum used to derive the mean, and the sample's own deviation) — not the same value being added twice into the same rollup.
- `o_10` (the mean) is consumed six times — once per sample's deviation subtraction. This is the expected broadcast of a single shared statistic (mean) into six independent deviation computations, not a duplicated financial entity.
- `o_11, o_13, o_15, o_17, o_19, o_21` (deviations) are each consumed twice, but both consumptions are as the `a` and `b` arguments of the *same* `multiply` operation (squaring: `dev * dev`). This is a mathematically necessary self-multiplication for computing squared deviation, not reuse across independent paths into a shared aggregate.
- The final aggregation `o_23 = addBulk(o_12, o_14, o_16, o_18, o_20, o_22)` sums exactly the six squared deviations, one per sample, with no repeated argument.
- `o_25 = o_23 / i_24` (degrees of freedom = 5 = n−1 = 6−1, correctly matching sample count `i_9` = 6) and `o_26 = sqrt(o_25)` complete a standard unbiased sample variance / standard deviation calculation.

## Details
This graph implements the canonical formula for sample variance and standard deviation: mean = ΣXᵢ/n; deviation_i = Xᵢ − mean; squared deviation_i = deviation_i²; variance = Σ(deviation_i²)/(n−1); stddev = √variance. The apparent "multiple consumption" flagged by the mechanical structural pass is fully explained by this formula's inherent structure — every sample legitimately participates in two distinct, non-overlapping computational roles (contributing to the mean, and being compared against the mean), and every deviation legitimately self-multiplies once to produce its square. Neither pattern feeds the *same* value twice into the *same* summation: the sum-of-samples aggregate (`o_8`) and the sum-of-squared-deviations aggregate (`o_23`) each incorporate every sample/deviation exactly once.

Manual re-computation of every intermediate and terminal value (sum = 80.1, mean = 13.35, each deviation and squared deviation, sum-of-squares = 7.3750, variance = 1.4750, stddev ≈ 1.214495780149112) matches the recorded values exactly, with no arithmetic drift indicative of a hidden tampering path. A check for Origin-ID/hash aliasing (distinct variable IDs secretly carrying the same underlying value) found all six raw sample values (12.5, 15.2, 11.8, 14.1, 13.6, 12.9) to be distinct, and no leaf/variable name collisions were found (consistent with the empty structural leaf-name-collision set). No cost/deduction entity was found netted into an intermediate subtotal and then subtracted again from a later aggregate.

Consequently, no violation of the stated invariants (path multiplicity, deduplicated-sum matching, alias-masking, double-netted deductions) was substantiated. This is a well-formed, internally consistent variance/standard-deviation computation over six titration replicate measurements, not a topological accumulation / double-counting fraud.
